nodes.Name: insertionSort_func
nodes.DocComment: insertionSort_func sorts data[a:b] using insertion sort.

nodes.Name: siftDown_func
nodes.DocComment:
siftDown_func implements the heap property on data[lo:hi].
first is an offset into the array where the root of the heap lies.

nodes.Name: pdqsort_func
nodes.DocComment:
pdqsort_func sorts data[a:b].
The algorithm based on pattern-defeating quicksort(pdqsort), but without the optimizations from BlockQuicksort.
pdqsort paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.05123.pdf
C++ implementation: https://github.com/orlp/pdqsort
Rust implementation: https://docs.rs/pdqsort/latest/pdqsort/
limit is the number of allowed bad (very unbalanced) pivots before falling back to heapsort.

nodes.Name: partition_func
nodes.DocComment:
partition_func does one quicksort partition. Let p = data[pivot] Moves elements in data[a:b] around, so that data[i]

=p for inewpivot. On return, data[newpivot] = p

nodes.Name: partitionEqual_func
nodes.DocComment:
partitionEqual_func partitions data[a:b] into elements equal to data[pivot] followed by elements greater than data[pivot].
It assumed that data[a:b] does not contain elements smaller than the data[pivot].

nodes.Name: partialInsertionSort_func
nodes.DocComment: partialInsertionSort_func partially sorts a slice, returns true if the slice is sorted at the end.

nodes.Name: breakPatterns_func
nodes.DocComment:
breakPatterns_func scatters some elements around in an attempt to break some patterns
that might cause imbalanced partitions in quicksort.

nodes.Name: choosePivot_func
nodes.DocComment:
choosePivot_func chooses a pivot in data[a:b].

[0,8): chooses a static pivot.
[8,shortestNinther): uses the simple median-of-three method.
[shortestNinther,∞): uses the Tukey ninther method.

nodes.Name: order2_func
nodes.DocComment: order2_func returns x,y where data[x] <= data[y], where x,y=a,b or x,y=b,a.

nodes.Name: median_func
nodes.DocComment: median_func returns x where data[x] is the median of data[a],data[b],data[c], where x is a, b, or c.

nodes.Name: medianAdjacent_func
nodes.DocComment: medianAdjacent_func finds the median of data[a - 1], data[a], data[a + 1] and stores the index into a.

nodes.Name: symMerge_func
nodes.DocComment:
symMerge_func merges the two sorted subsequences data[a:m] and data[m:b] using
the SymMerge algorithm from Pok-Son Kim and Arne Kutzner, "Stable Minimum
Storage Merging by Symmetric Comparisons", in Susanne Albers and Tomasz
Radzik, editors, Algorithms - ESA 2004, volume 3221 of Lecture Notes in
Computer Science, pages 714-723. Springer, 2004.

Let M = m-a and N = b-n. Wolog M < N.
The recursion depth is bound by ceil(log(N+M)).
The algorithm needs O(M*log(N/M + 1)) calls to data.Less.
The algorithm needs O((M+N)*log(M)) calls to data.Swap.

The paper gives O((M+N)*log(M)) as the number of assignments assuming a
rotation algorithm which uses O(M+N+gcd(M+N)) assignments. The argumentation
in the paper carries through for Swap operations, especially as the block
swapping rotate uses only O(M+N) Swaps.

symMerge assumes non-degenerate arguments: a < m && m < b.
Having the caller check this condition eliminates many leaf recursion calls,
which improves performance.

nodes.Name: rotate_func
nodes.DocComment:
rotate_func rotates two consecutive blocks u = data[a:m] and v = data[m:b] in data:
Data of the form 'x u v y' is changed to 'x v u y'.
rotate performs at most b-a many calls to data.Swap,
and it assumes non-degenerate arguments: a < m && m < b.
